title: Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning - CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning - Needs & Market Analysis
subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: Which of the following describes the primary purpose of conducting a spend analysis?
options: To ensure that all previous contracts were legally compliant.
To audit vendor invoices for overcharges.
To examine historical purchasing data to identify patterns, evaluate supplier consolidation, and discover cost-saving opportunities.
To determine the exact budget available for the next fiscal year.
questions.explain: Spend analysis is the process of collecting, cleansing, classifying, and analyzing expenditure data with the primary goal of decreasing procurement costs, improving efficiency, and monitoring compliance.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: An agency is choosing between purchasing a heavy-duty dump truck and leasing it. Which of the following factors most strongly supports the decision to LEASE rather than buy?
options: The agency requires a high degree of customization on the vehicle.
The technology and emissions standards for the trucks change rapidly, causing high obsolescence risk.
The agency has a surplus of capital funds that must be spent immediately.
The truck will be used extensively for 15 years with minimal maintenance expected.
questions.explain: Leasing is highly advantageous when equipment is prone to rapid technological obsolescence, as it allows the agency to upgrade equipment more frequently without the burden of disposal.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: In Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analysis, which of the following is considered an indirect, often 'hidden' cost?
options: The initial purchase price of the equipment.
Shipping and installation fees.
Internal training time for agency staff to learn the new equipment.
Monthly service agreement fees clearly stated in the contract.
questions.explain: TCO goes beyond the acquisition price. Staff training time represents an internal, indirect cost that impacts the true overall cost to the agency, even though it isn't a direct invoice from the supplier.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: A school district currently operates its own fleet of school buses (Make/Insourcing) but is considering outsourcing this to a private transportation company (Buy/Outsourcing). Which is a primary consideration for deciding to Make rather than Buy?
options: Outsourcing will retain absolute control over day-to-day route modifications and driver management.
Insourcing requires no capital investment in vehicle maintenance facilities.
The district wishes to maintain direct, total operational control over student safety and daily transportation logistics.
Private companies generally have higher economies of scale for fleet insurance.
questions.explain: Maintaining direct control over a sensitive or critical operation (like student safety and driver oversight) is a strong justification for insourcing ('Making') rather than outsourcing.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: According to the Pareto Principle (the 80/20 rule) in spend analysis, a buyer will typically find that:
options: 80% of the agency's vendors supply 20% of the services.
80% of total procurement spend is attributed to approximately 20% of the agency's suppliers.
80% of purchase orders are placed within the last 20% of the fiscal year.
80% of contracts will require 20% of the buyer's time to manage.
questions.explain: The Pareto Principle applied to spend analysis generally shows that a small number of suppliers (approx. 20%) account for the vast majority (approx. 80%) of the organization's total spend.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: Using supply positioning (such as the Kraljic Matrix), standard office supplies characterized by low risk/low complexity and low relative expenditure are classified as:
options: Strategic commodities.
Leverage commodities.
Routine (or non-critical) commodities.
Bottleneck commodities.
questions.explain: In the Kraljic Matrix, items with low supply risk and low profit impact (expenditure) are classified as Routine or Tactical items, where the goal is typically to simplify the acquisition process (e.g., using p-cards).
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: A buyer is evaluating a highly specialized laboratory chemical that has a very low expenditure level but is available from only one supplier worldwide, making the supply risk extremely high. In a supply positioning matrix, this is a:
options: Leverage item.
Routine item.
Bottleneck item.
Strategic item.
questions.explain: Bottleneck items have low financial impact but high supply risk. They are characterized by limited supplier availability or unique specifications, requiring strategies to ensure continuity of supply.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: A jurisdiction is purchasing complex HVAC systems. The buyer calculates the acquisition cost, operating energy costs, estimated maintenance, and eventual disposal cost. This calculation methodology is best known as:
options: Price Analysis.
Value Engineering.
Life Cycle Costing (LCC).
Target Costing.
questions.explain: Life Cycle Costing evaluates the total cost of an asset over its entire life span, factoring in acquisition, operation, maintenance, and end-of-life disposal costs.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: During market research for a new roof on a county building, the buyer looks at general market indices like the Producer Price Index (PPI). What is the primary purpose of tracking the PPI in this scenario?
options: To verify the prevailing wage laws for construction workers.
To anticipate pricing trends for construction materials like steel and asphalt.
To ensure that local minority-owned businesses are available.
To determine the architectural firm's profit margins.
questions.explain: The Producer Price Index (PPI) measures the average change over time in the selling prices received by domestic producers. Buyers use it to understand market conditions and anticipate material price fluctuations.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: What term describes unauthorized purchases made by an agency's employees outside of established, negotiated procurement contracts?
options: Maverick spend.
Strategic sourcing.
Aggregated spend.
Emergency spend.
questions.explain: Maverick spend refers to buying outside of established contracts or procedures, often resulting in higher prices, lost volume discounts, and compliance risks.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: A buyer has identified that several different departments are separately buying janitorial services. The buyer decides to consolidate these needs into one solicitation. This strategy is known as:
options: Unbundling.
Demand aggregation.
Market segmentation.
Value engineering.
questions.explain: Demand aggregation combines the requirements of multiple departments or units into a single procurement to leverage economies of scale and secure better pricing and terms.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: Which of the following scenarios best justifies an agency choosing an 'Operating Lease' over a 'Capital Lease' for IT equipment?
options: The agency wants ownership of the equipment at the end of the lease term.
The agency wants to record the lease as an asset and a liability on its balance sheet.
The equipment has a very short useful life before technological obsolescence, and the agency wants to return it after 3 years.
The equipment is custom-built and has no secondary market value.
questions.explain: An operating lease is essentially a rental agreement for a short term relative to the asset's life. It protects the lessee from obsolescence risk, making it ideal for fast-changing IT equipment.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: Value Analysis is typically performed to:
options: Re-evaluate an existing product or service to see if the same function can be performed at a lower cost without degrading quality.
Eliminate the lowest bidders from a competitive procurement.
Analyze the financial stability of a prospective supplier.
Determine the legal framework required for a contract.
questions.explain: Value Analysis is a systematic review of an existing product, service, or process aimed at identifying and eliminating unnecessary costs without compromising necessary function or quality.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: While conducting market research, a public buyer notices that the industry for a required service is highly fragmented, with many small regional suppliers and no dominant national players. This finding primarily suggests that:
options: A single national contract strategy will likely fail and a regional/multiple-award strategy may be required.
The agency should sole-source the requirement to the closest vendor.
Prices are likely to be monopolistic and tightly controlled.
The buyer must use a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) rather than an Invitation for Bids (IFB).
questions.explain: A fragmented market means no single vendor has the capacity to cover broad geographic areas. Therefore, a multiple-award or regionally divided contract strategy is often the most practical approach.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: An agency is evaluating whether to hire in-house mechanics to service its fleet or to contract out the service. When performing a 'Make vs. Buy' cost analysis, which cost should NOT be factored into the 'Make' (in-house) option?
options: Wages and fringe benefits of the mechanics.
Cost of building or renting a maintenance garage.
The profit margin typically charged by an external commercial mechanic.
Tools and diagnostic equipment required for the work.
questions.explain: Profit margin is inherently part of the 'Buy' (outsourcing) price because external vendors are for-profit. It is not an internal cost incurred if the agency decides to 'Make' (perform in-house).
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: During pre-solicitation planning, a buyer notes that end-users across different departments are requesting similar laptops, but with slightly varying, non-critical features. To achieve the best market pricing, the buyer should implement:
options: Standardization.
Customization.
Value Engineering.
Spot buying.
questions.explain: Standardization establishes an agreed-upon set of specifications across an organization. It reduces variation, simplifies maintenance, and allows the agency to aggregate volume for better pricing.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: A procurement office is projecting the quantity of road salt needed for the upcoming winter. They analyze usage quantities from the past five winters. This technique is known as:
options: Qualitative forecasting.
Time-series (Historical) demand forecasting.
Supply base analysis.
Make vs. Buy analysis.
questions.explain: Time-series forecasting relies on historical data points collected over time to project future demand, based on the assumption that past patterns will roughly continue or exhibit observable trends.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: If market research indicates an oligopoly structure for a specific commodity (few suppliers dominating the market), a buyer should anticipate:
options: Intense price-cutting competition and an abundance of substitute goods.
Limited price competition and potential barriers to new suppliers entering the market.
Complete willingness of suppliers to customize their products to agency demands.
Easy identification of localized, small business vendors.
questions.explain: An oligopoly consists of a small number of sellers. They often have significant market power, resulting in less aggressive price competition and high barriers for new market entrants.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: What is the key difference between Value Engineering (VE) and Value Analysis (VA)?
options: VE only looks at material costs, while VA only looks at labor costs.
VE is typically applied during the design phase to optimize cost and function before production, whereas VA is applied to redesign an existing product or service.
VE is performed by suppliers, whereas VA is only performed by the public buyer.
There is no difference; the terms are perfectly synonymous in public procurement.
questions.explain: Value Engineering (VE) is a proactive approach applied at the design stage. Value Analysis (VA) is a reactive approach applied to analyze an existing product or service.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: A buyer is mapping their agency's expenditures to standardized commodity codes (like NIGP or UNSPSC codes). The primary benefit of this action is to:
options: Facilitate accurate spend analysis by categorizing exactly what the agency is buying.
Ensure that the agency only buys from local vendors.
Prevent vendors from filing bid protests.
Eliminate the need to issue formal solicitations.
questions.explain: Standard commodity codes categorize items consistently across the organization. This consistency is essential for accurately running reports and conducting reliable spend analysis.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: During an initial market assessment for cloud storage solutions, a buyer discovers that standard commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) products will satisfy 95% of the agency's needs, while a fully custom solution would satisfy 100% but at triple the cost. The buyer's most prudent recommendation is to:
options: Recommend the custom solution because government needs must always be met 100%.
Suggest revising the agency's operational needs to adapt to the COTS product, recognizing the massive cost avoidance.
Abandon the procurement entirely and keep files exclusively in paper format.
Use an Invitation for Bids (IFB) to force developers to build the custom software at COTS prices.
questions.explain: Procurement often involves managing stakeholder requirements. Recommending a shift toward COTS software when the fit is extremely high saves significant time and taxpayer money, a core principle of value.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: In a Lease-or-Buy analysis, the 'discount rate' or 'cost of capital' is used to:
options: Calculate the vendor's prompt payment discount.
Determine the present value of future cash flows to accurately compare financial options over time.
Estimate the depreciation of a vendor's delivery vehicle.
Calculate the administrative cost of issuing a purchase order.
questions.explain: Because lease payments are made over time and a purchase is often a lump sum, financial analysis requires calculating the Net Present Value (NPV). The discount rate determines the present value of those future lease payments.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: Which of the following describes 'Price Analysis' in contrast to 'Cost Analysis'?
options: Evaluating the individual components of profit, labor, and materials overhead.
Comparing the vendor's total bottom-line proposed price against historical prices, published catalogs, and competitors' prices.
Conducting an audit of the vendor's internal accounting systems.
Applying Value Engineering to reduce the structural weight of a building.
questions.explain: Price analysis evaluates the total bottom-line price offered by comparing it against external benchmarks (other bids, catalogs, market prices). Cost analysis breaks down the individual elements of a price (labor, materials, profit).
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: To effectively reduce 'maverick spend' identified during a spend analysis, a centralized procurement department should:
options: Increase the limit on petty cash funds for all departments.
Implement user-friendly, organization-wide contracts for common items and restrict unauthorized vendor setup in the payment system.
Refuse to pay invoices for unauthorized purchases, permanently damaging supplier relationships.
Decentralize all purchasing authority down to the lowest level.
questions.explain: Reducing maverick spend requires making the 'right' way to buy the easiest way (via user-friendly, term contracts) while implementing system controls (restricting unauthorized P.O.s and vendor payments).
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning

questions.q: Market research reveals that the supply of a critical raw material is highly constrained due to recent international trade tariffs. How should this information influence the pre-solicitation strategy?
options: The buyer should shorten the solicitation period to secure a vendor immediately.
The buyer should write specifications to allow for acceptable substitute materials where feasible.
The buyer should use a Firm-Fixed Price contract strictly prohibiting any price adjustments.
The buyer should ignore the international news since the agency buys locally.
questions.explain: When raw materials are highly constrained, strict specifications can lead to excessively high bids or no bids. Allowing for acceptable substitutes mitigates supply chain risk and increases competition.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain II: Pre-Solicitation Planning
